comparison.objective: PR-520’s versions cap or press-fit-seal a cocktail shaker, agitate its contents, avoid spillage, return it upright, and in later versions reopen it. The candidate instead sets and locks an industrial gripper’s opening stop at 90° and verifies that setting through repeated actuation.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-520 tests bimanual shaker containment, tipping, oscillatory motion, press-fit sealing, and separation. The candidate tests coaxial driver and thin-wrench seating, coupled screw/jam-nut adjustment, countertorque that preserves a calibrated setting, tool withdrawal, and articulated functional testing. Generic bimanual holding is the only notable shared primitive.
comparison.success_condition: PR-520 grades shaker tilt and axial reversals, retained beads or spill volume, seal/open state, ice travel or mixing, and final upright placement. The candidate grades released opening-angle error, nut seating and retention, hands-off tool clearance, repeated return accuracy, and stop drift. No material rubric details are missing from the latest PR-520 spec; earlier versions omit some later press-fit/opening mechanics but still define numeric shake, loss, and upright thresholds.
comparison.reason: The tested ability and outcome are meaningfully different: dynamic containment and press-fit drink mixing do not exercise calibrated screw-and-locknut counterholding or retained mechanical-stop verification.
